subject.title: Improve context overflow error message with specifics

question: Which diagnostic fields may OpenClaw expose in channel-visible context-overflow messages, and which token source is authoritative enough to label as usage rather than an estimate?
rationale: Raw session identifiers can disclose routing data and token counters can be stale or provider-dependent, so implementation should not choose the public disclosure and accuracy contract implicitly.

options.title: Redacted diagnostics
options.body: Show a redacted display label, provider/model, effective limit, and observed-or-estimated usage with explicit qualifiers while keeping raw identifiers, paths, and payloads in logs.

options.title: Actions-only message
options.body: Keep visible text limited to recovery actions and expose detailed diagnostics through logs or a dedicated status/doctor surface.

options.title: Full identifiers
options.body: Show raw session identifiers and exact-looking counts in channel messages while intentionally accepting the privacy and accuracy tradeoffs.

recommendation.title: Redacted diagnostics
recommendation.body: Show a redacted display label, provider/model, effective limit, and observed-or-estimated usage with explicit qualifiers while keeping raw identifiers, paths, and payloads in logs.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent work spans the runner, recovery behavior, diagnostics, and auto-reply boundary where this contract must be applied consistently.
